Usage: assembly-differ <namespace|command> [options]

 (default command)
   Compares every library project in the current directory with the latest release of its package. Runs when no command is given.

   It reads the one solution in the directory, or else the project files in it, and skips test projects and projects
   with IsPackable set to false. It compares each project's Release build, for its newest target framework, with the
   latest stable release of its package on the feeds your NuGet.config lists. It does not build: run
   dotnet build -c Release first, and a project without build output is skipped with a warning. A project whose
   package has no release yet is reported and skipped. It needs the .NET SDK, to read the projects.

Global options:
  -h, --help  Show help.
  --version   Show version.

Commands:
  api           Writes the public API of a build as .api files, or checks
                committed ones against it.
  files         Compares two local builds: dlls, directories of dlls, or .nupkg
                files.
  nuget         Compares two versions of a package; in a solution, the version
                your projects use with another.
  projects      Compares every library project in the current directory with the
                latest release of its package. Runs when no command is given.
  pull-request  Puts a report on the pull request a GitHub Actions run is for:
                the job summary, one comment kept up to date, and the release
                label for the suggested version change.
  release       Compares a new build with the release before it.
  upgrades      Lists the packages a solution references that have a newer
                release, and what updating each would break.

Usage: assembly-differ files <old> <new> [options]

   Compares two local builds: dlls, directories of dlls, or .nupkg files.

Arguments:
  <old>  The old build: a .dll, a directory or a .nupkg.
  <new>  The new build: a .dll, a directory or a .nupkg.

Global options:
  -h, --help             Show help.

Options:
  --framework <string>   The target framework to take from a .nupkg, such as net8.0. Defaults to the newest both packages ship. [default: null]
  -t, --target <values>  [repeatable] Only compare these assemblies, by file name without extension. Repeat it for more than one.
  -f, --format <string>  The report: markdown, xml, asciidoc, github-comment or json. [default: markdown] [allowed: markdown|xml|asciidoc|github-comment|json]
  -o, --output <string>  A directory or file to write the report to, besides the console.
  --fail-on <enum>       Exit with code 4 when the suggested version change is at least this; none never fails. [default: none]
                         One of: <none|patch|minor|major>

Examples:
  assembly-differ files bin/1.2.0/MyLib.dll bin/1.3.0/MyLib.dll

  assembly-differ files MyLib.1.2.0.nupkg MyLib.1.3.0.nupkg --framework net8.0

result.stdout:
Usage: assembly-differ nuget <package> [<version>] [<new-version>] [options]

   Compares two versions of a package; in a solution, the version your projects use with another.

Arguments:
  <package>        The package id.
  [<version>]      With one version, the version to update to; with two, the old one. [default: null]
  [<new-version>]  The new version, when the old one is given too. [default: null]

Global options:
  -h, --help             Show help.

Options:
  --framework <string>   The target framework to compare, such as net8.0. In a solution, defaults to the one each project compiles against. [default: null]
  --all                  In a solution, show every change, not only the ones to API your built projects use.
  -t, --target <values>  [repeatable] Only compare these assemblies, by file name without extension. Repeat it for more than one.
  -f, --format <string>  The report: markdown, xml, asciidoc, github-comment or json. [default: markdown] [allowed: markdown|xml|asciidoc|github-comment|json]
  -o, --output <string>  A directory or file to write the report to, besides the console.
  --fail-on <enum>       Exit with code 4 when the suggested version change is at least this; none never fails. [default: none]
                         One of: <none|patch|minor|major>

Notes:

  In a directory with a solution or project files, nuget X compares the version of X your projects resolve with
  its latest stable release, and nuget X 2.0.0 with 2.0.0: what updating would change. It reads the resolved version,
  and the target framework each project compiles X for, from obj/project.assets.json, so restore first. When projects
  resolve different versions, each is compared. In a solution it shows only the changes to the types and members your
  built projects reference, the ones that affect you, unless --all is set; build first. Members match by name, and a
  constant you use does not show, because the compiler copies its value into your code. Give two versions to compare
  them anywhere.

Examples:
  assembly
[truncated]

Usage: assembly-differ pull-request <report> [options]

   Puts a report on the pull request a GitHub Actions run is for: the job summary, one comment kept up to date, and the release label for the suggested version change.

Arguments:
  <report>  The api-changes.json a command wrote with --format json.

Global options:
  -h, --help              Show help.

Options:
  --repository <string>   The repository as owner/name; defaults to GITHUB_REPOSITORY. [default: null]
  --pull-request <value>  The pull request number; defaults to the one in GITHUB_EVENT_PATH. [default: default]
  --fail-on <enum>        Exit with code 4 when the suggested version change is at least this, unless the pull request has the allow label; none never fails. [default: none]
                          One of: <none|patch|minor|major>
  --allow-label <string>  The label that allows a change at --fail-on, so the check passes; empty allows none. [default: breaking-allowed]
  --major-label <string>  The label for a Major change, matching release-drafter's; empty sets none. [default: breaking]
  --minor-label <string>  The label for a Minor change; empty sets none. [default: feature]
  --patch-label <string>  The label for a Patch change; empty sets none. [default: ]
  --no-comment            Leave the comment alone.
  --no-labels             Leave the labels alone.

Notes:

  Run a command with --format json first; this reads the api-changes.json it writes. The comment is found again by a
  hidden marker and updated, and the labels this tool set are recorded in it: a later run swaps only those, never a
  label a person added. It needs GITHUB_TOKEN with pull-requests: write. Without write access, as on a pull request
  from a fork, it writes the job summary, warns and succeeds; outside a pull request it writes the job summary only.
  With --fail-on, a change at that level fails the check until someone adds the allow label, breaking-allowed by
  default; the workflow has to run on the labeled and unlabeled events too, so adding the label runs it a
[truncated]

Usage: assembly-differ release <path> [options]

   Compares a new build with the release before it.

Arguments:
  <path>  The new build: a .nupkg, a .dll or a directory.

Global options:
  -h, --help             Show help.

Options:
  --package <string>     The package id; read from a .nupkg when not given. [default: null]
  --version <string>     The version being released; read from a .nupkg when not given. [default: null]
  --framework <string>   The target framework to compare, such as net8.0. Defaults to the newest the .nupkg ships. [default: null]
  --require-baseline     Fail when there is no earlier release to compare with.
  -t, --target <values>  [repeatable] Only compare these assemblies, by file name without extension. Repeat it for more than one.
  -f, --format <string>  The report: markdown, xml, asciidoc, github-comment or json. [default: markdown] [allowed: markdown|xml|asciidoc|github-comment|json]
  -o, --output <string>  A directory or file to write the report to, besides the console.
  --fail-on <enum>       Exit with code 4 when the suggested version change is at least this; none never fails. [default: none]
                         One of: <none|patch|minor|major>

Notes:

  Give a .nupkg and the package id and version come from it; for a .dll or a directory, pass --package and --version.
  The release compared with is the newest stable one before that version, on the feeds your NuGet.config lists.
  Without one, this is a first release: there is nothing to compare, and the command succeeds unless
  --require-baseline is set.

Examples:
  assembly-differ release build/output/MyLib.1.3.0.nupkg --fail-on major

  assembly-differ release src/MyLib/bin/Release/net8.0 --package MyLib --version 1.3.0 -t MyLib

Usage: assembly-differ upgrades [options]

   Lists the packages a solution references that have a newer release, and what updating each would break.

Global options:
  -h, --help             Show help.

Options:
  --all                  Count every change, not only the ones to API your built projects use.
  -f, --format <string>  markdown, a table, or json. [default: markdown] [allowed: markdown|json]
  -o, --output <string>  A directory or file to write the report to, besides the console. [default: null]
  --fail-on <enum>       Exit with code 4 when an update's change to the API your code uses is at least this; none never fails. [default: none]
                         One of: <none|patch|minor|major>

Notes:

  It reads the packages every project in the directory references directly, as obj/project.assets.json resolves them,
  so restore first. Each one with a newer stable release on your NuGet.config feeds is compared with it, the way
  nuget X is: only the changes to API your built projects use count, unless --all is set, so build first. Use
  assembly-differ nuget X to see one package's changes in full.

Examples:
  dotnet build && assembly-differ upgrades
